subject: MAP cadence compression and contingency schedule
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: need options to compress evaluation after IT audit delay

Mina,

Quick note from my side — our internal security audit got pushed by two weeks (unexpected scope expansion). That pauses our hands-on evaluation (SRE + privacy signoff) and puts the June 30 close target at risk.

Procurement is already asking for a revised mutual action plan and dates. We need suggestions from your side on how to compress the MAP without sacrificing the core eval gates (latency SLA test, data retention check, SOC2 evidence review).

Can you:
- propose a compressed set of checkpoints we can commit to?
- call out any gating items that cannot be shortened?
- confirm whether Redwood can support a split canary (subset of traffic) during the evaluation week?

Attaching the current timeline we gave procurement. If we can't keep close in late June we'll likely slip into mid-July which creates knock-on budget approvals.

Thanks,
Liam

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP: need options to compress evaluation after IT audit delay

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear about the audit slip. We can compress the MAP but want to make the trade-offs explicit. Below are two options and a short risk log.

Option A (2-week compression — conservative):
- Keep all original gates, shorten owner review windows (3 business days each)
- Run parallel security docs review (we'll provide SOC2 excerpts + KMS diagram same day)
- Can run a limited canary (non-prod traffic replay) during the first week
- Net effect: target close ~2027-07-07 if you confirm by Mon 5/17

Option B (aggressive compression — 1-week):
- Combine latency + functional smoke into a single 48-hour test window
- Redwood provides pre-signed audit artifacts and a dedicated infra SME for live triage
- Canary: production-like traffic for a single customer segment (read-only)
- Net effect: target close ~2027-06-30 if procurement signs off by Tue 5/18 and procurement accepts limited PO terms

Key gating items (cannot be shortened easily):
- Full SOC2 report delivery (we can provide SOC2 excerpts and a letter of attestation, but final report timing is fixed)
- Customer network whitelist changes (these depend on your IT change window)

Risk log (high level):
- R1: Procurement delay on PO approval -> push close >= +2 weeks. Owner: Acme procurement.
- R2: Network whitelisting window missed -> prevents canary. Owner: Acme network ops.
- R3: Regression in quantized model path during stress run -> requires extra hotfix window. Owner: Redwood infra (we'll pre-allocate SME).

I've attached a compressed MAP template (acme_map_v3.1.xlsx) with proposed dates and owners (yellow highlights). If you prefer, we can brief procurement together on Monday to speed approvals.

Propose a quick call Monday 08:30 PT to lock Option A vs B and sign off owners.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Mina — thanks for the clear options. Two quick notes from procurement:
1) Procurement needs a one-page statement of work & milestone schedule to attach to the PO.
2) They will ask for a contingency credit if we move to the aggressive path (Option B) because the shortened windows raise internal risk.

Andrew (copied) will lead on the PO side.

If Redwood can provide a short escalation note for leadership (to support expedited approvals) and confirm a canary scope (customer segments X and Y only), we can likely target Option B and keep the June 30 close.

I'll join a Monday call.

-Liam

On a separate note: can you put the one-page SOW and an executive escalation blurb into the Drive link you mentioned so procurement can pick it up?

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Hi all — looping in briefly from my side (Sales Director).

We authorize the following to avoid a full slip:
- One-time contingency credit up to $5,000 if Acme agrees to the aggressive Option B and signs PO by Tue 5/18 EOD.
- Redwood will assign an infra SME (Monica) to be on-call during the compressed test window.
- Canary scope: customer segments X (read-only) and Y (<=5% traffic) only; no write paths.

Risks:
- If network whitelisting misses the requested slot, the credit is void and schedule moves to the next window.
- If SOC2 final report is required for procurement signoff, we will provide an attestation letter but final close may require the full report; plan accordingly.

- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/1234567

- M5 (Final exec signoff): Acme + Redwood -> target Tue 2027-06-30
